_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the two-channel risk classifier (docs/MCP/Classifier/risk-trigger-classifier-design.md). Canonical: mcp_server/risk_signals.json; vendored byte-identical copy: plugin/hooks/risk_signals.json (synced by scripts/sync_risk_classifier.py, enforced by tests/test_classifier_sync.py). Edit signals/weights/thresholds HERE only.

signals.name: hardcoded_secret
signals._comment: Phase 5b C2 (coverage expansion, paper Domain 2): added vendor-prefixed key formats (Google AIza [audit F-001 initially added the new AQ. prefix too, but advisor 2026-07-09 REVERTED it: `AQ\.[0-9A-Za-z_-]{20,}` false-floored `AQ.SOME_LONG_CONSTANT` (a 2-char prefix + `.` member-accessor collides with a static access / a module named AQ) — an auto-trigger FLOOR that's never test-exempt = the highest-consequence FP. AIza covers existing/legacy keys; re-add AQ. only with its VERIFIED exact key structure/length (Phase-6/5c tracked)], Slack xox[baprse]- [audit F-008: e = enterprise-grid], OpenAI sk-(proj|None)- [audit F-002: sk-None- = user-associated keys created outside a project], GitLab glpat-) as NEW auto-trigger FLOOR patterns — high-entropy distinctive prefixes with near-zero cross-language FP (like the existing sk_live_/ghp_/AKIA/PEM). value_filter_patterns:[5] still points at the GENERIC key=value pattern (index 5) — NEW patterns are APPENDED after it so that index is unchanged; DO NOT insert a pattern before index 5 (it would silently break the value filter — audit F-007). NOT added here (advisor 2026-07-09): JWT literals (eyJ… — often a PUBLIC/example token, not a secret; secrets are never test/docs-exempt so it'd floor every example → a separate non-floor `jwt_literal` advisory below) and SA-JSON `"type":"service_account"` (a config MARKER, not a secret value — the real credential is the inline PEM private_key, which already floors).

signals.name: jwt_literal
signals._comment: Phase 5b C2 (coverage expansion): a JWT literal (eyJ<b64>.eyJ<b64>.<sig>) — ADVISORY (significance/10, NON-floor), NOT part of hardcoded_secret (advisor 2026-07-09): a JWT is frequently a PUBLIC/example token (docs, tests, decoded-payload demos), and since secrets are NEVER test/docs-exempt, flooring it would block every fixture/example. A LEAKED session JWT is a real secret, but the FP rate on the literal shape is too high for a floor — surfaced as a self-skippable LOW advisory instead. Three base64url segments (header.payload.signature) with the JWT `eyJ` header prefix, so a bare base64 blob does not fire.

signals.name: auth_security
signals._comment: STRONG auth signals only (Phase 6 specificity stratification). Specific auth verbs/decision-flags/credential nouns/protocol names/decorators/imports — each self-sufficient for HIGH on the floor class. The AMBIGUOUS nouns (session/login/logout/permission/privilege/role), which are common identifiers, live in the borderline-class `auth_surface` signal below and never reach HIGH alone (they need a strong co-signal — corroboration). gitleaks composite-rule pattern. See docs/MCP/gate skip solve/PHASE6-DESIGN.md.

signals.name: auth_surface
signals._comment: WEAK auth nouns commonly used as ordinary identifiers (session/login/logout/permission/privilege/role). Borderline-class significance, NON-floor category (auth_surface is intentionally absent from gate_fire_models.FLOOR_CATEGORIES). Fires a LOW advisory checkpoint alone; reaches HIGH only when a strong auth_security signal co-occurs (corroboration). Stacked weak nouns never escalate (one signal, weight 10). skeleton_match[0] keeps an in-string/comment match blanked. Plurals are matched (permissions/roles/privileges/sessions) — audit F-001 closed a pre-existing \b plural gap; this is a recall gain (still LOW non-floor). snake_case compounds (role_id, user_role) intentionally do NOT match (audit F-004 — even lower auth likelihood, less noise).

signals.name: billing
signals._comment: Phase 4 B3 (coverage expansion): NAMED-SDK ONLY floor. The ambiguous money nouns (charge|refund|payout|invoice|subscription|checkout|price_id|line_item) were REMOVED from this floor and the money-domain ones folded into the non-floor `financial_custom` advisory (deliberated mcp_4b23ca82: bare nouns fail the precision axis of the joint floor principle — `checkout` floored `actions/checkout`, a tracked FP now fixed). A named payment SDK (stripe/braintree/paypal/adyen/chargebee, Stripe::, import stripe) is near-zero-FP and stays a FLOOR. Webhook-signature-verification / idempotency-key REMOVAL is the sibling `billing_control_removed` floor (match:removed). Custom (non-SDK) money mutation now only advises via financial_custom — accepted gap (paper §1: no SDK name = no precise floor). skeleton_match[0] blanks an in-string/comment SDK-name mention.

signals.name: billing_control_removed
signals._comment: Phase 4 B3 (coverage expansion; Mechanism M1 and_not_added): removal of a payment-integrity control — a webhook SIGNATURE VERIFICATION (Stripe `Webhook.constructEvent`/`construct_event`, generic `verify_webhook_signature`/`verify_signature`/`validate_signature`) or an IDEMPOTENCY KEY (`idempotency_key`/`idempotencyKey`) — NOT re-added anywhere in the file (refactor-safe via and_not_added, like pii_redaction_removed). FLOOR (category billing), test/docs-EXEMPT (billing is in _FLOOR_EXEMPT_TEST_DOCS). High consequence: dropping webhook-sig verification enables forged-event replay; dropping the idempotency key enables double-charges. WEIGHT 36 > max non-floor trigger (30 post-Phase-4) for the deciding-category tie. Removal-only, so a benign refactor that renames+re-adds the control does not fire.

signals.name: migration_destructive
signals._comment: Phase 4 B2 (coverage expansion): the DESTRUCTIVE/integrity-affecting subset of the old all-migrations `migration_schema` floor — the only migration shapes that pass the joint severity-AND-precision floor test (deliberated mcp_4b23ca82). DROP TABLE/SCHEMA/DATABASE (audit F-002: schema/database more catastrophic than a table), DROP COLUMN, TRUNCATE TABLE, DROP INDEX/CONSTRAINT/FK/PK, + ORM destructive equivalents (Alembic op.drop_*, ActiveRecord remove_column/remove_index/remove_foreign_key/drop_table, Knex/Prisma dropTable/dropColumn/dropForeign/dropIndex, Django migrations.DeleteModel/RemoveField — audit F-001, the primary Django destructive forms; without them a Django RemoveField migration would miss the floor now that migration_path no longer floors). Matches RAW lines (NO skeleton_match — SQL DDL lives inside op.execute("...") string literals; skeletonizing would blind it). FLOOR (category migration_destructive in FLOOR_CATEGORIES), test/docs-EXEMPT (a DROP in a test fixture is scaffolding). WEIGHT 36 > max non-floor trigger (30 post-Phase-4) for the deciding-category tie. OUT OF SCOPE (documented, paper §1 detectable-only): type-narrowing + NOT-NULL-without-default (need old-vs-new column comparison) and DML data-mutation in migrations (DELETE/UPDATE — high FP on legit backfills; owner ruling 2026-07-09) are NOT floored — they surface via the migration_additive advisory. `TRUNCATE table` requires the TABLE keyword (bare `TRUNCATE foo;` is a minor documented gap) to avoid the .truncate() method FP.

signals.name: migration_destructive_removed
signals._comment: Phase 4 B2 (coverage expansion; Mechanism M1 and_not_added): a DESTRUCTIVE schema-evolution expressed as a REMOVAL — removing an Alembic/Rails `downgrade()` (the migration can no longer be rolled back) or removing a proto2 `required Type name = N;` field (a breaking wire-schema change). Refactor-safe via and_not_added (a moved/renamed downgrade re-added in the same file does not fire). FLOOR (category migration_destructive), test/docs-EXEMPT. Non-relational schema-evo that needs old-vs-new comparison (proto field-NUMBER reuse, avro compat, ES mapping type change) is OUT OF SCOPE (semantic — paper §1); only the lexically-sharp REMOVAL forms floor. downgrade and proto-required live in disjoint file types (.py vs .proto), so the pattern-set-wide and_not_added suppression can't cross them.

signals.name: migration_additive
signals._comment: Phase 4 B2 (coverage expansion): ADDITIVE / recoverable schema changes — the non-destructive remainder of the old `migration_schema` floor. ADVISORY (significance/10, non-floor category migration_additive): fires LOW (surfaced, self-skippable), can NEVER reach HIGH by the two-channel cap. CREATE TABLE/INDEX, ADD COLUMN, db.Column/mapped_column, FOREIGN KEY, Alembic op.create_*/add_column/alter_column/rename_column, ActiveRecord add_column/add_index/change_column/add_reference. This is the intended contract flip (paper Domain 5: additive → advisory): a previously-HIGH-floor additive migration now fires LOW. NO skeleton_match (SQL DDL inside op.execute string literals must match).

signals.name: migration_path
signals._comment: Phase 4 B2 (coverage expansion): DROPPED from floor to a LOW path advisory (deliberated mcp_4b23ca82: the path floor was a blunt proxy for content risk — living under migrations/ is not itself dangerous; a destructive DROP is caught by migration_destructive CONTENT). Now class:domain weight 10 category migration_additive (non-floor) — a migration file fires a LOW visibility advisory by path, and the FLOOR rests entirely on destructive content patterns.

signals.name: dangerous_exec
signals._comment: Phase 1 A4 precision fix + Phase 5c D2 (polyglot lookbehind): the bare eval/exec patterns use `(?<![.\w>])(?<!::)` so a METHOD call does NOT fire — `.exec()` (JS regex `re.compile(...).exec(s)`, the original FP), PHP `$obj->exec()` (the `>` of `->`), and C++/Ruby `Cls::exec()` (the `::`) are all suppressed, while a bare `exec(user_code)`/`eval(x)` still fires. D2 detail (Phase-1 note): the `::` uses a 2-char lookbehind so a SINGLE colon is NOT excluded — Python `lambda:exec(x)` (dangerous) still fires (its 2 preceding chars are `a:`, not `::`); only the C++/Ruby double-colon static call is suppressed. Node's `child_process.exec` keeps its OWN dedicated pattern below (it needs the `child_process.` literal). Accepted minor FN: a bare exec right after `>` (`=>exec`/`a>exec`, no space) is suppressed — rare, and the real Node case has its own pattern.

signals.name: iac_public_exposure
signals._comment: Phase 4 B4 (coverage expansion): PROMOTED non-floor→FLOOR (category iac_exposure added to FLOOR_CATEGORIES; deliberated mcp_4b23ca82, unanimous). The patterns were ALREADY the sharp low-FP sub-cases (0.0.0.0/0 ingress, wildcard IAM Action/Principal, S3 public-read, privileged container, runAsUser:0) — near-zero legit FP in production infra + catastrophic exposure = passes the joint severity-AND-precision floor test. WEIGHT stays 35: once iac_exposure is a floor, the max REMAINING non-floor trigger is 30, so 35 already wins the deciding-category tie (no 36 bump needed). TEST/DOCS-EXEMPT (in _FLOOR_EXEMPT_TEST_DOCS): a misconfig in a test FIXTURE is not shipped infra; a `0.0.0.0/0` in a README doesn't fire at all (prose exclusion skips non-auto content signals on .md/.rst/.txt).

signals.name: financial_custom
signals._comment: Phase 1 A1 (coverage expansion, paper Domain 6): custom money/ledger domain logic — the non-Stripe world the named-SDK `billing` floor misses. ADVISORY (significance/10, non-floor category): LOW alone, rides to HIGH only when a real money TRIGGER (billing, 30) co-fires on the same hunk (emergent corroboration — no new mechanism). Full aggressive noun set incl. the ambiguous amount|price|cost|balance|fee|tax|discount (Q2: small advisory FP acceptable — a physics `balance` fires LOW, the agent skips). By two-channel construction a significance signal can NEVER reach HIGH alone, so aggression here can't manufacture a false BLOCK. skeleton_match[0] keeps a keyword-in-prose/string/comment blanked. English identifiers only (Q9 documented scope limit).

signals.name: pii
signals._comment: Phase 1 A2 (coverage expansion, paper Domain 7): PII exposure surface — the whole domain absent today. ADVISORY (significance/10, non-floor): LOW alone, cannot escalate by construction. Patterns match RAW lines (they look INSIDE string literals — email/card literals — so intentionally NO skeleton_match, exactly like the secret signal). Credit-card is SEPARATOR-GROUPED shapes only (reviewer fix, mandatory): a bare 13-19-digit run is NOT Luhn and FPs on epoch-ms timestamps (1783561690428), DB IDs, phone numbers; true Luhn is not regex-expressible, so we require the 4-4-4-4 / 4-6-5 grouping. Email is QUOTED-only (a literal), dodging the `@decorator` FP. PII-name-into-log-sink catches identifiers flowing to a log/print call. Prose paths (.md/.txt) skip this (content signal, non-auto-trigger). The masking-REMOVAL FLOOR is a separate Phase-3 signal (needs M1 refactor-safety).

signals.name: injection_surface
signals._comment: Phase 1 A3 (coverage expansion, paper Domain 3): injection SINK-SHAPE breadth beyond SQL — SSRF, path-traversal, XSS, shell=True, template-injection. trigger/25 blocks at HIGH under focused (like the existing sql_injection_surface) but NON-floor -> self-skippable (paper §1: injection is sink-presence not taint-flow, so never floored). Each pattern is SHAPED to the DANGEROUS form so the default library idiom does NOT fire: SSRF+XSS (owner ruling 2026-07-08, paper Domain 3 'request-derived URL' over the plan's looser 'variable URL') require an INBOUND-REQUEST-DERIVED token (request./req.query|body|params/$_GET.../user_input/DOM location.*) inside the sink — so `requests.get(url)`, `innerHTML=this.value`, AND the outbound-construction idioms `requests.get(url, params=query)`/`post(url, json=payload)` stay SILENT (bare params/payload are OUTBOUND kwargs, NOT taint — dropped from the token set), while `requests.get(request.args[..])` / `innerHTML=req.body.x` BLOCK. Path-traversal requires a literal `../`; template-injection requires string concat; shell=True is the dangerous flag itself. Mirrors sql_injection_surface's `.*\+` shaping discipline.

signals.name: ci_cd
signals._comment: Phase 1 A5 (coverage expansion, paper Domain 19). ADVISORY (significance/10, non-floor): flags CI/CD-risk SHAPES THE AGENT WRITES (incl. under prompt injection) — explicitly NOT a CI/CD security guarantee (layer2_dependent, paper §4b: external-PR / human-authored / merge-time coverage is owed to the unbuilt Layer-2 merge gate, and Domain 19 is first in line for it). Patterns are GitHub-Actions/Dockerfile-shaped so they self-scope to CI files without a path-gate mechanism (mutable-tag action refs, permissions:write-all, curl|sh, Dockerfile ADD <url>). The secret-echo FLOOR is a separate Phase-2 signal. Prose paths skip this.

signals.name: ci_secret_echo
signals._comment: Phase 2 A5-F (coverage expansion, paper Domain 19): a CI secret echoed to logs/artifacts — echo/printf of a `${{ secrets.* }}` value (dot OR bracket access: secrets.NAME / secrets['NAME'] / secrets["NAME"] — audit F-005). `printenv` was dropped (audit N-004: it prints an env var by NAME and does not evaluate `${{ }}`, so `printenv ${{ secrets.X }}` isn't a real leak shape — near-zero recall, only FP noise). FLOOR (category ci_secret_echo in FLOOR_CATEGORIES) and a HARD floor EVERYWHERE — deliberately NOT in _FLOOR_EXEMPT_TEST_DOCS (advisor 2026-07-08): .github/workflows/* classifies as test_or_docs, so exempting it would defeat the floor in the very files it targets; it follows the secrets precedent (a CI secret leak must not be judgment-skippable). SEPARATE category from the Phase 1 advisory `ci_cd` (flooring ci_cd would floor the mutable-tag/curl|sh advisories). WEIGHT 36 > the max non-floor trigger weight (iac_public_exposure=35) so it wins the single-deciding-category selection even when a non-floor trigger co-fires on the same line (audit F-002). Matches RAW lines (no skeleton — like the secret signal, it must look inside string literals, e.g. `run: echo "...${{ secrets.X }}"`), so a commented-out `# echo ${{ secrets.X }}` also fires (audit N-003 — a conservative FP, clearable via confirm_floor; comment-stripping would blind the real in-string case). Per-line matching (no DOTALL), so echo + secrets on DIFFERENT lines never co-match (audit F-006). layer2_dependent (paper §4b).

signals.name: unsafe_deserialization_ml
signals._comment: Phase 2 (coverage expansion, paper Domain 18): unsafe ML model deserialization — CWE-502 RCE on load. FLOOR (category unsafe_deserialization_ml in FLOOR_CATEGORIES), EXEMPT on test/docs paths (in _FLOOR_EXEMPT_TEST_DOCS — ML test suites load fixtures with joblib constantly; a test fixture doesn't ship as prod logic). JOBLIB.LOAD ONLY (owner ruling 2026-07-08, advisor-confirmed): joblib.load is an unambiguous pickle-RCE vector with no safe mode -> a clean, precise FLOOR. torch.load is DELIBERATELY NOT here — PyTorch 2.6+ made `weights_only=True` the default so bare torch.load is safe-by-default, and `weights_only=False` is LEGITIMATELY required for full-checkpoint loads, so NO torch.load form is a precise floor signal (paper §1: floor = severity AND precision). torch.load stays a LOW advisory via the existing ml_data_domain (surfaced, self-skippable, never floored). This dissolves the audit's F-001 (nested-paren lookahead) + F-003 (2.6 default) entirely — there is no torch pattern. WEIGHT 36 > max non-floor trigger (35) so joblib wins the deciding-category selection when a non-floor trigger co-fires on one line, e.g. exec(joblib.load(x)) (audit F-002). pickle.load is untouched (non-floor deserialization_untrusted).

signals.name: ci_pwn_request
signals._comment: Phase 3 (coverage expansion, paper Domain 19; Mechanism M1 all_of). A GitHub Actions PWN-REQUEST: a `pull_request_target`/`workflow_run` trigger (runs with repo secrets) combined, in the same workflow file, with a CHECKOUT of the untrusted PR head (arbitrary code exec with secrets in scope). FLOOR (category ci_pwn_request in FLOOR_CATEGORIES), a HARD floor EVERYWHERE — deliberately NOT test/docs-exempt (like ci_secret_echo: .github/workflows/* classifies as test_or_docs, so exempting it would defeat the floor in the files it targets). THREE all_of groups (owner ruling 2026-07-08, audit F-001/F-002 precision): (g0) a CHECKOUT step must be present — `uses: .../checkout` or `git checkout` — so a NON-checkout action that merely takes a `ref:` param does NOT floor; (g1) the untrusted-head REF — `ref: ...head.(sha|ref)` / `github.head_ref`, anchored `^(?!\s*#)` to EXCLUDE commented-out lines and NOT match a bare labeling/status mention; (g2) the pwn TRIGGER. all_of two-stage: fires on a NEW workflow file (all groups in one hunk) OR an EDIT (the added checkout step + pre-existing trigger confirmed via the file_content_fetcher; no fetcher/failed read -> fail-safe fire). Recall boundary (documented): an exotic custom checkout action without the word `checkout` is missed. WEIGHT 36 > max non-floor trigger (35) for the deciding-category tie (ties among equal-weight triggers break by JSON declaration order — deterministic). layer2_dependent (paper §4b): the AGENT-authored slice (incl. under prompt injection); external-PR/human/merge-time is Layer 2's job.

signals.name: pii_redaction_removed
signals._comment: Phase 3 (coverage expansion, paper Domain 7; Mechanism M1 and_not_added). Removal of a PII masking/redaction call (mask/redact/anonymize/scrub/pseudonymize/deidentify) that is NOT re-added anywhere in the same file's diff — a PII-protection regression before a log/export sink (GDPR/CCPA-severe, irreversible in log aggregators). FLOOR (category pii_redaction_removed in FLOOR_CATEGORIES), test/docs-EXEMPT (in _FLOOR_EXEMPT_TEST_DOCS — a masking-call removal in a test fixture is not a prod PII leak; same logic as auth/billing/unsafe_deser, NOT secret-adjacent). REFACTOR-SAFE via and_not_added (Mechanism M1): a rename/move of the masking call (removed here, re-added anywhere in the file) does NOT fire — the whole reason M1 exists. WEIGHT 36 for the deciding-category tie. KNOWN residual: suppression is pattern-set-wide (remove field-A's mask + add field-B's mask suppresses; PHASE3-M1-DESIGN.md).

signals.name: removed_safety_control
signals._comment: Phase 5b (audit mcp_592b45d6 F-003): skeleton_match on pattern[0] ONLY (the stem list) — a removed PROSE/string/comment line (a removed log `"request validated"` or a doc-comment) must NOT floor now that the auth/validation stems match compounds/inflections (validate->validated); skeleton blanks comments/strings so only removed CODE fires. Pattern[1] (the `if .*SINK` guard) is DELIBERATELY NOT skeletonized: the sink keyword is LEGITIMATELY a string literal in a real guard (`if role != "admin"`, `if scope == "payment"`), so blanking strings there would lose the match (a phase6 regression proved it — advisor 2026-07-09). Accept the rare `# if not authorized`-comment FP on pattern[1] (clearable) to keep the common string-keyword guard. Phase 5c: pattern[2] (skeletonized, index 2) adds framework auth-CALLBACK removals the stems miss — login-based (login_required/require_login/logged_in?/signed_in?), Rails `before_action :...login`, and WordPress (current_user_can/wp_verify_nonce/check_admin_referer/is_user_logged_in — surfaced by the real WP CVEs CVE-2025-68861 / CVE-2026-11364, whose auth-check removal the stems + verify_ underscore-prefix both missed). These are auth-REMOVAL floors (Domain 1: floor on removal, not addition — the added-auth case stays advisory). Phase 4 B1 (coverage expansion): pattern[1] — the same-line `if .*(SINK)` guard-removal detector — was BROADENED beyond auth to payment/secret/critical-state sinks, folding in the coverage the demoted `removed_conditional` soft-floor used to provide (deliberated mcp_4b23ca82 + owner sign-off 2026-07-09; PHASE4-DESIGN.md §2). The EXISTING auth sub-alternation `\b(auth|admin|permission|valid|allow|denied|forbidden)\b` is byte-UNCHANGED (no regression); the NEW payment/secret/critical stems use a LEADING `\b` and NO trailing boundary so they match snake_case compounds a real guard names — `if not payment_authorized(...)`, `if secret_key_present` (the common form) — while the leading `\b` still excludes `repayment`/`prepayment`. The BLEED-PRONE stems (token/secret/charge/quota) carry a `(?=[\W_]|$)` lookahead (audit F-004): it still allows a `_`/`.`/space continuation (token_id, secret_key, charge.verify) but blocks an ALPHA continuation, so `tokenizer`/`secretary`/`charger`/`quotation` no longer false-floor; the plainer stems keep bare no-trailing-boundary (they don't bleed into a common word) and so still match their plurals. SAME-LINE (not file-wide M1) chosen deliberately: M1 unions matches file-wide and would floor an unrelated removed `if` in one hunk + an unrelated `payment` token in another — the desensitization vector. RECALL COST (documented, accepted): (a) a guard whose CONDITION does not name the sink (`if feature_enabled:` wrapping a removed `process_refund()`) is missed; (b) a sink at the TAIL of a snake_case compound (`has_valid_token`) is missed by the leading `\b` — the dot-access / standalone / leading-compound forms fire. The file-wide alternative's cross-hunk false-floor is strictly worse. Removed-line context keeps FP low. `checkout` and `audit` are deliberately EXCLUDED (checkout = the actions/checkout FP source + a payment-flow noun; audit-removal is Phase-6 D1). pattern[0] (bare safety-verb removal) is unchanged.

signals.name: idor_scoping_removed
signals._comment: Phase 5b C1 (coverage expansion, paper Domain 1 §108; Mechanism M1 and_not_added). Removal of a multi-tenancy SCOPING predicate from a surviving query — a `.filter(...tenant_id`/`.where(...org_id`/`default_scope`/`belongs_to_tenant` dropped → IDOR/BOLA (OWASP API1). ADVISORY (significance/10, NON-floor), NOT a floor (deliberated mcp_c2e4e9cd, 4/4 + owner sign-off 2026-07-09): the load-bearing token is an ENGLISH identifier (tenant_id/org_id) — §4a-1 demotes noun-lists to advisory — and the rename/refactor false-'fire' is STRUCTURALLY guaranteed (tenant_id→tenantId, extract-scope-to-a-concern which is cross-FILE so and_not_added's file-scope misses the re-add, .where(account_id:)→.for_account) so a FLOOR here would desensitize. and_not_added keeps a same-FILE rename refactor-safe. Requires the scoping-CALL shape (not a bare tenant_id mention). NO path_gate (path_gate is mutually exclusive with M1 in v1; an advisory firing on a non-query file is low noise). Surfaced with the API1 reference.

signals.name: observability_removed
signals._comment: Phase 6 D1 (coverage expansion, paper Domain 11; Mechanism M1 and_not_added). Removal of an AUDIT/compliance-event emission — a forensic-integrity/compliance gap (SOX/HIPAA/PCI audit trail). ADVISORY (significance/10, NON-floor), NOT a floor (owner ruling 2026-07-09 via AskUserQuestion, ratifying the paper's 'floor when adjacent to a financial/auth event' as advisory): structurally identical to the multi-tenancy case the 4-model panel ruled advisory (5b) — audit/log are file-wide-fuzzy adjacency + a recoverable consequence (not an irreversible catastrophe), so a floor would desensitize. SCOPED to audit/compliance-SPECIFIC tokens ONLY (advisor 2026-07-09) — NOT bare log/event/track (those are so common that even a LOW advisory becomes noise on every removed debug line, which erodes the gate). and_not_added keeps a same-file rename refactor-safe. Surfaced with a SOX/HIPAA/PCI audit-trail note.
signals._comment2: audit mcp_69540af8 F-003/F-005 (documented, advisory-level so no code change): `SecurityEvent` is the most collision-prone token (a generic domain-event class / protobuf type / Spring ApplicationEvent isn't an audit emission) — kept because a removed SecurityEvent emission IS plausibly a security-audit removal and this is a self-skippable LOW advisory; demote if telemetry shows noise. and_not_added is FILE-scoped, so a cross-FILE import move of AuditLog defeats it (advisory FP on a pure import reorg) — inherent M1 limitation.

signals.name: memory_safety_sink
signals._comment: Phase 5a (coverage expansion, paper Domain 15; Mechanism M2 context). SELF-PRECISE C memory-corruption sinks — gets/strcpy/strcat. FLOOR (category memory_safety in FLOOR_CATEGORIES), PATH-UNCONDITIONAL BY INVARIANT (the loader FORBIDS path_gate on a floor: path-gating a floor is a silent bypass — a strcpy in a .inc/.go.tmpl/extensionless file would escape). These pass the joint severity-AND-precision floor test (paper §1): catastrophic (`gets` was REMOVED from C11 — no safe use; strcpy/strcat = the canonical exploitable-buffer-overflow class) AND self-precise (they don't appear as meaningful cross-language tokens, so firing everywhere is low-FP — unlike free()/malloc() which are common method names, path-gated as ADVISORIES below). TEST/DOCS-EXEMPT (memory_safety in _FLOOR_EXEMPT_TEST_DOCS — a strcpy in a fixture is scaffolding; the test_path suppressor also demotes). WEIGHT 36 > max non-floor trigger (30) for the deciding-category tie. Documented honest-FP: `strcat` as a string-concat name in some DSLs (FP-acceptable per Q2, cleared by confirm_floor). unsafe.Pointer/unsafe{ are NOT here (a legitimate low-level capability, not a known-bad sink) — they stay the ffi_unsafe ADVISORY. `gets` REQUIRES AN ARGUMENT (`\bgets\s*\(\s*[^)\s]`) — audit mcp_e3c0edf8 F-5a + owner ruling 2026-07-09: bare `\bgets\s*\(` collided with Ruby's stdin read (`gets()`, `input = gets.chomp`); C `gets(buf)` always passes a buffer, so requiring a non-empty first arg keeps the C floor while dropping the Ruby FP (Ruby `gets()`/bare `gets`/`gets.chomp` no longer match; a rare Ruby `gets(sep)` still floors, clearable). stpcpy/wcscpy/wcscat added (owner ruling — C/C++-only unbounded-copy siblings of strcpy, no cross-language collision). skeleton_match on ALL patterns (advisor 2026-07-09): these are CODE-CALL shapes, so blank comments/strings/JSX first — a `// replaced strcpy() with strncpy()` remediation comment or a `"don't use strcpy("` doc-string must NOT floor a developer doing the right thing (a real strcpy call is always code, so zero recall loss; matches the auth/billing floor discipline). deliberated mcp_98973ec2 + owner sign-off 2026-07-09; PHASE5A-M2-DESIGN.md.

signals.name: ffi_unsafe
signals._comment: Phase 5a: the SELF-PRECISE (path-UNCONDITIONAL) FFI/unsafe surface — advisory (primitive/8). The C-memory method-call patterns (memcpy|malloc|free|memmove|alloca) were SPLIT OUT to the path-gated `ffi_unsafe_c_memory` sibling below (Mechanism M2) because bare `\bfree\s*\(` false-positived cross-language on JS `pool.free()` / Python `self.free()`. NEW: `\bunsafe\.Pointer\b` (Go — previously fired nothing; self-precise so path-unconditional, and ADVISORY not floor: a legitimate low-level Go capability, not a known-bad sink). volatile stays here unconditional (a keyword; a future increment may path-gate it if the prose/Java FP matters).

signals.name: ffi_unsafe_c_memory
signals._comment: Phase 5a (Mechanism M2 path-gate DEMONSTRATOR); EXTENDED Phase 5b C3. The common-word C-memory + unsafe-format/input functions (memcpy|malloc|free|memmove|alloca + sprintf|vsprintf|scanf|sscanf) ARMED only on C-family files. Same category `ffi_unsafe` (no categorization change) — this SPLIT exists purely so M2 can path-gate these patterns to fix the confirmed cross-language FP (JS `pool.free(buf)`, Python `self.free(key)` fired ffi_unsafe unconditionally before; PHP/Python `sprintf` is safe/common and must not fire). ADVISORY (primitive/8, NON-floor — the loader would REJECT a floor carrying path_gate). 5b C3: sprintf/scanf are NOT floored (advisor + the floor-never-path-gated invariant) — unlike gets/strcpy they CAN'T get the arg-trick (PHP sprintf takes args too) and collide cross-language, so they're path-gated advisories, not floors. path_gate regexes are END-OF-STRING anchored (`\.c$`, not `\.c` which also matches `.css`/`.c.orig`). C-family = .c/.h/.cc/.cpp/.cxx/.hpp/.hh/.hxx/.cu + .cuh (CUDA header) + .m/.mm (Objective-C/C++) — audit mcp_e3c0edf8 F-2a/3a/3b added the CUDA-header + Objective-C forms.

signals.name: reflection_dynamic
signals._comment: Fix 4 P-c (A4): getattr/setattr fire ONLY when the attribute arg is NON-CONSTANT (a variable/expr), not a string literal. getattr(o, 'x')/setattr(o, 'x', v) are plain, safe attribute access — the reproduced A4 false positive. getattr(o, name)/setattr(o, field, v) and f-strings (getattr(o, f'x{n}')) stay dynamic. Deferred imports and ORM .update never matched here (verified). This is a LEXICAL heuristic on a NON-floor advisory category, so a few accepted blind spots (audit mcp_1242df66): (1) a dynamic expr that BEGINS with a string literal — getattr(o, 'p_' + f) — is suppressed [recall gap]; (2) matching is line-by-line, so a MULTILINE call whose comma sits on a separate line fires nothing [minor recall loss, no spurious fire]; (3) r/b-string attrs (getattr(o, r'x')) still fire [residual noise]. All tolerated because dynamic_code never floors.

signals.name: mobile_domain
signals._comment: Phase 6 (residual Tier-2, paper Domain 16): added self-precise Android insecure-WebView / insecure-storage tokens — ADVISORY (domain/12, non-floor, path-UNCONDITIONAL: these are Android-specific identifiers with no cross-language collision, so no M2 path-gate needed). DIRECTIONAL: setJavaScriptEnabled / setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs / setAllowFileAccess require `(true)` so the fix-direction `(false)` does NOT fire (same discipline as InsecureSkipVerify). MODE_WORLD_READABLE/WRITEABLE (world-accessible file storage) is inherently insecure.

signals.name: tls_pinning_removed
signals._comment: Phase 5b C4 (coverage expansion, paper Domain 16; Mechanism M1 and_not_added). Removal of a TLS certificate-PINNING enforcer (OkHttp `CertificatePinner`, iOS `NSPinnedDomains`, `serverTrustPolicy` pinning) — opens a MitM surface. FLOOR (category tls_pinning_removed in FLOOR_CATEGORIES; deliberated mcp_c2e4e9cd + owner sign-off 2026-07-09), SELF-PRECISE vendor tokens only so it fires PATH-UNCONDITIONALLY (a floor is NEVER path-gated) with near-zero cross-language collision. Bare `pinning`/`sslPinning`/`certPinning` are DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED (they collide with UI/version/thread/message pinning). and_not_added keeps a same-file rename refactor-safe. NOT test/docs-exempt (panel: accept the rare TrustAll test-mock FP, cleared by confirm_floor). WEIGHT 36 for the deciding-category tie. Directional: this is the enforcer-REMOVAL half; the bypass-ADDITION half is `tls_pinning_bypass` below.

signals.name: tls_pinning_bypass
signals._comment: Phase 5b C4 (coverage expansion, paper Domain 16). The bypass-ADDITION half of the cert-pinning floor (category tls_pinning_removed): ADDING a TLS trust bypass — iOS `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads` (disables ATS), Android/Java `TrustAllHostnameVerifier`/`TrustAllCerts`/`ALLOW_ALL_HOSTNAME_VERIFIER`, Go `InsecureSkipVerify: true`. FLOOR, SELF-PRECISE (distinctive vendor tokens, path-unconditional). Directional: fires on ADDITION (adding a bypass is the risk; removing one is a fix). WEIGHT 36. `InsecureSkipVerify` requires `true` to avoid matching a `false` (safe) assignment.

signals.name: embedded_safety_disable
signals._comment: Phase 5b C4 (coverage expansion, paper Domain 17; Mechanism M2 path-gate). Disabling an embedded SAFETY control — watchdog/interlock disable. ADVISORY (domain/12, NON-floor) + PATH-GATED to firmware/C paths (deliberated mcp_c2e4e9cd + owner sign-off 2026-07-09): `watchdog`/`interlock` are NOT self-precise (systemd `WatchdogSec`, pytest-timeout, process supervisors, deploy/CI interlocks all collide), so this CANNOT be a path-unconditional floor — it's a path-gated advisory instead. The SELF-PRECISE MCU register tokens (IWDG_KR/WWDG_CR/WDT_FEED/esp_task_wdt_delete) ARE floor-worthy but a NEW floor category → flagged for Phase 5c with its own sign-off (advisory here). Safety-LIMIT constant changes (MAX_TEMP raised) are SEMANTIC (need old-vs-new) → out-of-scope, like type-narrowing. Only the disable-CALL shape is lexical.

suppressors.name: test_path
suppressors._comment: Phase 5c C5 (suppressor polyglot parity): added _(test|spec)\.(...|rs) so Ruby RSpec `_spec.rb` (THE Ruby test convention) + Rust `_test.rs` suppress like Go/Py/Java (a mis-named prod source file `foo_spec.rb` is not a real convention, so this suppresses only genuine test paths). C++ gtest / Swift Tests/ already covered by the tests?/spec dir prefix.

suppressors.name: generated_vendor_path
suppressors._comment: Phase 5c C5: `\.generated\.` catches the codegen convention (Login.generated.dart, App.generated.cs) + added dart/go. The UNDERSCORE form `_generated.` was DROPPED (audit mcp_b6a3c2 F-003: `report_generated.go` is a plausible HAND-WRITTEN filename that would then over-suppress a real floor to silent; `_generated` is not a strong codegen convention).
